Inflammatory Pseudotumor: The patient's symptoms of cough producing bloody mucoid sputum and anorexia, as well as the chest radiograph and CT scan findings of a peripheral opacity in the right lung and a soft tissue density mass in the right lower lobe, could be consistent with inflammatory pseudotumor. The microscopic findings of fibroblasts, collagen, and inflammatory cells mainly of lymphocytes and plasma cells also support this diagnosis.
Bronchiectasis: The patient's symptoms of cough producing bloody mucoid sputum, anorexia, and history of intermittent upper respiratory tract infections are consistent with bronchiectasis. The physical examination finding of reduced breath sounds at the right lung base and the laboratory tests showing normochromic-normocytic anemia, low serum iron levels, and an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate also support this diagnosis. The chest radiograph and CT scan findings of a peripheral opacity in the right lung and a soft tissue density mass in the right lower lobe are also consistent with bronchiectasis.
